pr_title: kubelet: Add a TopologyManager policy option: max-allowable-numa-nodes
pr_body:
Add a TopologyManager policy option for kubelet, which can make maxAllowableNUMANodes in the kubelet's TopologyManager configurable.

Hi @PiotrProkop @ffromani Could you please take a look?

The changes looks good to me. I just think we need KEP for this effort(should be pretty straightforward, I can help with the KEP if needed) and when it will be approved we can track this change for k8s 1.31 😄

> The changes looks good to me. I just think we need KEP for this effort(should be pretty straightforward, I can help with the KEP if needed) and when it will be approved we can track this change for k8s 1.31 😄

I agree (this is also something @swatisehgal highlighted e.g. in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124148#discussion_r1550133658). Either approaches - a new flag or a policy option are fine to me, but either will require some extra process as it stands today

> require some extra process as it stands today

Is the extra process a KEP or something else? I am willing to submit a KEP for this 😄

> > require some extra process as it stands today
> 
> Is the extra process a KEP or something else? I am willing to submit a KEP for this 😄

Regarding the extra process I was thinking to the API review for the flag addition. AFAIK the flag addition won't need a Feature Gate nor a KEP, at least not in the general case. If so, it will emerge during the API review I think.
For the policy option, it will require a KEP as the process stands today AFAIK.

EDIT: OTOH the new option can likely [start from beta stage](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/7828/commits/d060ec0d6e51f7f476f73975573924b87b3927df).

I still think this should be TopologyManager policy option, but we should have it start as an already-on beta feature according to the new policy. @cyclinder do you have the time / experience to put together a KEP for this? I'm happy to help review.

Here is an example for adding a similar policy option to the CPU manager. I would imagine this KEP to look similar:
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3334
Thanks @klueska! I'm interested in this and I'll spend the time understanding this.

In addition, if we start as beta, we should do some e2e changes. I'd start with a simple modularization: change the existing e2e tests to run once with default settings, and again the same tests with `maxAllowableNUMANodes = 2*default`. This is the most basic verification that the changed setting is not breaking stuff.
We are unlikely to ever hardware powerful enough to exercise > 8 NUMA Nodes (or just 4...), so this very basic validation is likely the best we can do in the short/mid term

>  if we start as beta, we should do some e2e changes. I'd start with a simple modularization: change the existing e2e tests to run once with default settings, and again the same tests with maxAllowableNUMANodes = 2*default

issue_context.title: Make maxAllowableNUMANodes in the kubelet's TopologyManager configurable
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add a config option to the `kubelet` that allows us to configure the value of `maxAllowableNUMANodes` in the TopologyManager:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/79c61d5f0305c566b642be978b1e4837870db257/pkg/kubelet/cm/topologymanager/topology_manager.go#L40

### Why is this needed?

The current hard-coded value of 8 was added as a stop-gap 4 years ago, with a plan to improve the topology manager to remove the state explosion that occurs when trying to enumerate the possible NUMA affinities and generating their hints (which unfortunately never happened).

The long term solution should be to refactor this code to avoid the state explosion altogether. In the meantime, a configurable option should be sufficient to allow users to increase the limit when appropriate.
comments:
/triage accepted
/priority important-longterm

Note: adding kubelet options/flags will require API review

I want to work on this, I will be assigning this to myself, let me know if you have any questions.

/assign

review_comments:
`TopologyManagerPolicyOptions` can set more than one option, Use `NewMapStringString` to pass multiple sets at the same time, commas separate them. see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/88313a445174e21ed326f40802429b854e5be9ba/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/cli/flag/map_string_string.go#L76-L90

And I've seen other similar kubelet flags that also use `NewMapStringString`, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/88313a445174e21ed326f40802429b854e5be9ba/cmd/kubelet/app/options/options.go#L497

please let me know If I'm wrong.
it seems a correct change, thanks for elaborating.

I'd keep this constant but renamed like `DefaultMaxAllowableNUMANodes` - if user doesn't specify a new value, this is the recommended default. The user should probably not be enabled to set less (what's the point?) but if they set more, they should IMO get a warning both in the logs and from the docs
That make sense, thanks for the comment.

> but if they set more, they should IMO get a warning both in the logs and from the docs

Can you tell me where this warning or log or docs would be better if they set more? thanks!

It's sufficient to add a `klog.Warning` call in `policy_options.go` for now.
When moving to GA we can evaluate more options (just brainstorming, something like a node condition)
we need to enable the TopologyManager Alpha-level policy options to make the current code work. But didn't we decide in the KEP to start from beta?
Yes, we start from beta, and why do we still need to enable the TopologyManager Alpha-level policy options here?
either works, but the best fix is to move the new option to beta.

We shouldn't have to, but you still have the option listed as an alpha feature here:

Isn't this new option already in beta? see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124148#discussion_r1558954149

IMO we can keep it like this.
